clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with 1-week subacute onset of painless left lower limb weakness and numbness. Physical examination revealed diffuse weakness involving multiple left lower limb muscle groups, diminished proprioception and pain perception distal to the mid-calf, and absent left ankle deep-tendon reflex. Eight days from symptom onset, gadolinium-enhanced MRI demonstrated bilateral cauda equina nerve root enhancement with sparing of the lumbosacral plexuses, and electrophysiological studies showed asymmetrically absent left tibial H-reflex, diminished left saphenous sensory response, and reduced recruitment in left vastus lateralis, gastrocnemius, and tibialis anterior consistent with plexopathy. Twelve days from onset, CSF analysis revealed cytoalbuminologic dissociation (protein 1.03 g/L with normal cell count of 1/μL) without oligoclonal bands. These findings established a diagnosis of inflammatory lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy in the absence of diabetes mellitus.
